title: Blood Loss Assessment after 3D Visualization in Robotic Hepatectomy
summary: Robotic liver surgery is increasingly used for the treatment of benign and malignant liver tumors. Although robotic surgery is associated with fewer complications compared to open hepatectomy, blood loss remains an important risk, especially during complex hepatectomies. Modern three-dimensional (3D) models of the liver may improve surgical planning by clearly showing the individual anatomy and the position of tumors. The BLADE trial therefore investigates whether the use of 3D models can further reduce blood loss during complex robotic liver surgery.
conditions: Malignant neoplasm of liver and intrahepatic bile ducts

interventions.name: Robotic complex hepatectomy with additional 3D liver reconstruction
Robotic complex hepatectomy without additional 3D liver reconstruction

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Elective complex robotic hepatectomies for benign or malignant lesions 
- Age equal to or greater than 18 years
- ASA I-III
- Written informed consent
Exclusion criteria:
- pregnancy and breastfeeding
- vascular reconstruction and/or extrahepatic resections
- Impaired mental state or language barrier
- Suspected lack of compliance
